text:
maria: quick upload of the end-to-end scan for KV quant modes. focused on 13B streaming decode with long prefixes (2k). putting the important bits here so we can triage.
ajay: thanks — did you run with the production kernel-policy=auto and adaptive batching?
maria: yes, auto kernels + adaptive window (latency-first). also ran fixed batch sizes 1 and 16 for baseline.
perf-bot: perf-scan start id=2026-03-18-009 models=[redwood/13b] hw=gpu-a100s scenarios=[streaming, chat]
liam: curious about memory vs latency tradeoffs. what were the peak KV footprints?
maria: summarized from the profiler:
```
mode      peak_kv_gb   avg_decode_ms   quality_delta_pct
fp8        5.8           40.6            -0.1
int8       3.1           46.5            -2.2
hybrid     4.4           42.0            -0.4
4bit       2.0           57.8            -3.9
```
naomi: so INT8 saves ~2.7GB but adds ~5.9ms and ~2.2% quality loss on our long-context eval. that matches prior instincts but larger quality gap than expected.
ajay: do we have token-level diffs for the largest drift?
maria: yes — pasted a trimmed trace from the failing session (streaming decode, turn 5):
```
ref: "She argued that the proposal required more study before adoption."
int8: "She argue that the proposal require more study before adoption ."
fp8: "She argued that the proposal required more study before adoption."
logits_l2_norm: 0.035   (layer 25 kv lookup)
kv_max_abs_err: 0.015
```
liam: 0.035 norm at a middle layer is pretty large, easy to accumulate over 20+ tokens. did you try per-head calibration?
maria: tried symmetric per-head scales during calibration (KV tensors only). that brought INT8 quality delta to -1.0% and latency down slightly (~+4.8ms). memory stayed ~3.3GB.
naomi: did you experiment with storing keys in fp8 and values in int8? keys look more critical for attention logits.
maria: yes — hybrid (keys=fp8, values=int8) run looks promising: decent memory win and much smaller quality impact. posted numbers above.
ajay: great. operational question: can the runtime pick hybrid dynamically? e.g., route requests with prefix_len>1024 to hybrid, else full-int8?
liam: we have routing hooks in the scheduler; adding a rule should be straightforward. need to ensure kernel-policy table includes hybrid kernel variants. also want microbench on int8-micro vs int8-gemm — Maria, can you attach the microbench?
maria: attached quick microbench:
```
seq_len=16: int8-micro 1.8ms, int8-gemm 1.4ms
seq_len=64: int8-micro 3.6ms, int8-gemm 3.0ms
seq_len=256: int8-micro 12.1ms, int8-gemm 10.7ms
```
liam: so microkernel is slower here, likely due to less fused post-ops and extra reorders. that explains part of the +4-6ms overhead we saw.
naomi: any effect from batching heuristics? long prefixes reduce batchability, so latency hit is more exposed.
maria: yes, adaptive batching window reduced throughput for long requests. A/B with fixed small batching (batch=1) gave similar quality deltas but slightly higher latency.
ajay: for rollout controls, we should gate kv quant changes behind a golden prompt eval: auto-fail if >1.0% quality regression on long-context bench. Also add telemetry flags to surface kv-mode per-customer.
maria: agreed. I'll open a PR with: (1) per-head KV calibration flags (2) hybrid kv-mode in kernel-policy matrix (3) rollout gate and ops telemetry. assigning to liam for kernel review.
perf-bot: perf-scan complete id=2026-03-18-009 duration=00:10:12 artifacts=s3://perf-scans/2026-03-18-009/
liam: will review the kernel policy changes and run extended microbenches on other hardware (v100 and 80GB a100).
naomi: please add a short note in the release notes so support teams can triage memory vs quality questions for dedicated customers.
ajay: also add an ops playbook: if a customer flips kv-quant to int8 and reports decode drift, recommend hybrid kv-mode or enable per-head calibration.
maria: creating the PR now with perf artifacts and the failing traces linked. thanks everyone.
